clue.text: Judges united: lawmakers must restrain anger

parts.note: U is a standard abbreviation for united, as in football club names

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the lawmakers' letters close around the anger

parts.note: MPs, Members of Parliament, make the laws
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: Referees banding together while parliament tries to keep its temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires adjudicate games, so they act as judges of play; the plural verb-noun swaps cleanly.

clue.text: Monkey doctor holding limb firm

indicators.note: one piece holding another means the second sits inside the first

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a doctor
an arm is a limb
set means firm, as jelly that has set

explanation.surface: A vet gripping an animal's arm tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American species of monkey.

clue.text: Still needing one minute on phone

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Someone stuck waiting for just a minute on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Immobile means not moving, which is one sense of still as an adjective.

clue.text: Long-running show possibly needs a rest

indicators.note: possibly suggests the words could be arranged another way, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A show that has run for decades might deserve a break.
explanation.walkthrough: EASTENDERS is a BBC television soap opera set in east London, running since 1985.
explanation.definitionFit: The soap has been broadcast continuously since the 1980s, making it a famously durable programme.

clue.text: Ultraviolet decay occasionally seen in eye part

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then means every other letter of decay is used

explanation.surface: Sun damage seen as decay in part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvea is the pigmented middle layer of the eyeball, including the iris.

clue.text: Magical character one supporting Black Country

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits below, so the other letters go underneath black

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rune is a letter of an old alphabet credited with magical power
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sorcerer propping up the industrial Black Country of the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is an industrial area of the West Midlands; here Black is only B and Country is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the island of Borneo, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Carbon and barium mixed in Carlisle region

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of barium are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemistry experiment combining two elements in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Barium looks set to give its symbol Ba, but the whole word is the anagram fodder. Carlisle is the county town of CUMBRIA, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle lies in this county of the English Lake District, so it is that city's region.

clue.text: Balance on board say amongst elite US Navy personnel

indicators.note: one piece placed amongst others sits inside them

parts.note: the SEALs are the US Navy's special forces
eg, for example, is what say means when introducing an example

explanation.surface: Keeping steady aboard ship, as with the US Navy's crack troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Having good sea legs means keeping one's footing on a moving ship's deck.

clue.text: Five entering rocky route on approach

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of route are shaken up

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
re means on, about, concerning

explanation.surface: Five travellers on a rough road coming closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is not a link here but RE, concerning; 'rocky' gives OERTU, which V enters.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening approach or proposal made to someone.

clue.text: Agreement favouring tightwad right to be cancelled

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: a letter to be cancelled is struck out of the word

parts.note: a miser is a tightwad

explanation.surface: A deal that suits a skinflint, whose rights get annulled.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise is an undertaking or pledge, a kind of agreement to do something.

clue.text: Chuck returning in waterway sees man-eater

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the waterway

parts.note: a canal is an artificial waterway

indicators.note: returning means the word for chuck is read backwards

parts.note: to bin something is to chuck it away

explanation.surface: A man named Chuck coming back along a canal meets a flesh-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck looks like a name but is the verb, discard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats human flesh, a literal eater of people.

clue.text: Cold fish — picture something to keep it fresh

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
the ling is a fish of the cod family
a film is a motion picture

explanation.surface: A cold fish photographed and wrapped to stay fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin plastic wrap seals food from the air so that leftovers stay fresh.

clue.text: With British mole shot outside Tobermory?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, around, the abbreviation for British
shot means wrecked, so the letters of mole are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British mole gunned down near Tobermory, a harbour town on Mull.
explanation.walkthrough: Tobermory is a Scottish town, but it is also the name of the handyman Womble in the British children's books and television series about litter-collecting creatures on Wimbledon Common.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobermory is one of the Womble characters, so the question mark marks him as an example.

clue.text: Very tense: keen on arrest

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so keen follows arrest

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to arrest them
a keen or biting wind is sharp

explanation.surface: Someone nervous because they're eager to make an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail-biting finish keeps spectators in suspense, so it describes a moment of high tension.

clue.text: Extra large notice to be dismantled? Vote

parts.note: a bye is an extra in cricket, a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart and rebuilt, so the letters of notice are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outsized poster being taken down after a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-election is a special vote held to fill one vacant parliamentary seat.

clue.text: Shelley's Inferno?

indicators.note: the possessive says the shorter word belongs to, and is held within, the poet's name

explanation.surface: A title for a poem by Shelley in the style of Dante.
explanation.walkthrough: Inferno suggests Dante's poem; the question mark flags that it is simply contained in the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is an Italian-derived word for the infernal regions, the place of eternal fire and damnation.

clue.text: Holly for instance always the ingénue?

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
an ingénue is naive and inexperienced, which is what green means

explanation.surface: Holly, a girl's name, forever cast as the innocent young actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly looks like an actress's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly keeps its leaves all winter, so it is an example of a plant that never sheds foliage.

clue.text: Dark scene — small number go bad in church

parts.note: No is the shortened form of number

indicators.note: in puts the spoiling word inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
milk that goes bad is said to turn

explanation.surface: A gloomy tableau of a congregation turning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a painting of a night scene, as in Whistler's nocturnes of the Thames.

clue.text: Huntress coming into bar finds Hoosier

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a bar
Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: A female hunter walking into a pub and finding a stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoosier is the nickname for a native of the American state of Indiana.

clue.text: Garden visitor in two arguments

parts.note: two arguments are wanted, and the first is spar, to argue as boxers do in practice
the second argument is a row, a noisy quarrel rhyming with cow

explanation.surface: A guest in the garden caught between two quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparrows are small birds that commonly visit gardens and bird tables.

clue.text: Disease sees lamb almost destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word lamb loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A farmer finds a lamb nearly killed by illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LAMB to LAM, and 'destroyed' rearranges SEES with LAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is a contagious viral illness causing a red rash.

clue.text: Beastly noise reason tattooist must stop?

definitions.meaning: a tattooist who has run out of ink must stop

explanation.definitionFit: A pig's grunting sound is the noise of a farmyard animal, a beast.

clue.text: Democrat among pine trees altered decree in advance

indicators.note: one letter placed among others goes inside them
altered means changed, so the letters of pine trees are rearranged

explanation.surface: A US politician in a forest changing an order beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges PINE TREES, and 'among' places D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To predestine is to ordain or determine a fate beforehand.

clue.text: Bug one way or another?

parts.note: the word is a bug in the insect sense and, as a verb meaning to eavesdrop, a bug in the listening sense

explanation.definitionFit: As an insect it is a creepy-crawly; as a verb it means to listen in secretly, like a planted microphone.

clue.text: Milk about to be brought round — moggies love it

parts.note: ca, circa, means about with dates

indicators.note: brought round means turned about, so the milk word is read backwards

parts.note: a pint is a measure of milk delivered to the doorstep

explanation.surface: Fetching the milk in for cats who adore it.
explanation.walkthrough: Moggy is British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb of the mint family has a scent that cats find irresistible.

clue.text: Perhaps an 18 can?

parts.note: 18 down is a native of an American state, and can is US slang for a toilet; what an American calls the lavatory

explanation.walkthrough: Can looks like a verb, but it is the American slang noun for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the polite word for a public toilet is this compound, so it is a lavatory for a US citizen.

clue.text: Concedes nothing — then three points!

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
W, N and S are three compass points: west, north and south

explanation.surface: A team conceding no goals and then taking three points from a win.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface of a win worth three points misleads; the points are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up, or own, is to admit or concede something, as in owning a mistake.

clue.text: Thrilling sensation cut short angry speech

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a vibe is a feeling or sensation
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: An exciting feeling interrupted by someone shouting furiously.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrant means full of energy and excitement, which is to say thrilling.

clue.text: Be on diet fixed and disciplined

indicators.note: fixed means rearranged or rigged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to stick to a diet and keep self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciplined person or animal follows orders and rules, which is being compliant.

clue.text: A new banknote should be announced, one feels

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the note's word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note in British slang

explanation.surface: An announcement that a new banknote is coming, which someone senses.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner, British slang for a ten-pound note, sounds like TENNA in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's antenna is a feeler, the organ it touches and senses with.
